The telecommunications sector is characterized by regulatory fragmentation, which requires providers to navigate varying frameworks that can delay infrastructure deployment [84] . Regional markets often present unique compliance requirements, licensing procedures, and municipal bylaws governing physical network installations, such as trenching for fiber-optic cables. This fragmentation compounds operational difficulties, as navigating these varying regulatory environments requires dedicated administrative resources and can lead to unpredictable project timelines [84] . Providers must maintain robust compliance strategies and foster cooperative relationships with local municipal authorities to mitigate the risk of regulatory delays.
